0fe40ac1e83d: Building a Calendar Time Slot Picker in Salesforce
32be8a96b2a3: What is a calendar time slot picker?
7ce19d88d150: A calendar where you choose a day, with a grid underneath that splits the day into bookable intervals. Slots that are already taken are shown as unavailable, so people only pick times that are free.
86bf8aa80a77: Does Salesforce have a time slot picker?
ed5f68564ca4: Not for your own objects. A standard Date/Time field is a date input plus a time dropdown, and it cannot see other records. MultiDatePick adds a time slot picker that reads existing bookings when the calendar loads and only offers what is free.
96f8d4deb05a: Can the time slots be any length?
a3f10e56968f: Yes. The slot interval is any number of minutes. 15, 30 or 60 minutes are typical, and a 45 minute interview slot works the same way.
0d6525f1bcca: Do I need Apex or a developer to add a time slot picker?
cb4a4613cc4d: No. The Setup Wizard writes the configuration, and the component goes on a record page, app page, Experience Cloud site or Screen Flow by setting Config Name. There is no code to write.
c0596f613070: Salesforce calendar time slot picker grid showing available and unavailable slots grouped by period
c441c56595ae: Salesforce gives you a date picker and a time field. It does not give you a grid of selectable slots. Here is what a real Salesforce time slot picker takes, and how to get one without building it.
587fb21654f2: A time slot picker is a specific interface: a calendar where you choose a day, and a grid underneath showing that day broken into bookable intervals, with the taken ones visibly unavailable. Everyone recognizes it, because every booking site on the internet uses it. Salesforce does not ship one.
41b22b062a53: Pick an advisor, a day and an open slot. Taken slots are never offered.
db72d9c55379: Drag across four days, drag 09:00 to 12:00, save one record per day.
00349900a353: A standard Date/Time field renders as a date input plus a time dropdown. It is a form control, and it has no idea what else is booked. Nothing stops a user selecting a slot that is already gone, because the field does not know other records exist. That check happens later, in a validation rule or a flow, after the user has already committed to a choice.
2025a52eb134: That is the gap. A time slot picker queries existing records <t1>before</t1> the user chooses, and only offers what is free.

7859f3f0226b: Why building it yourself is more work than it looks
48103198470d: The rendering is the easy part. These are the parts nobody scopes:
c1d3c812bbeb: Efficiently, without blowing governor limits when someone opens a two-month view.
64bab3aeee31: Fiddly the moment bookings can be different lengths.
ad7e49fcb2ef: The running user's timezone and the record's are not always the same.
52cd1ee9af62: Two people looking at the same free slot at the same moment.
41a56630a109: The component has to respect what the running user can see.
1a5e366cd3ad: A grid of clickable divs is not keyboard navigable by default.
8e14c31445a8: Accessibility needs the most care. A slot grid needs proper ARIA grid semantics, arrow-key navigation, and a state that is conveyed by more than color. It is the part most in-house builds skip, and the part a procurement review asks about.
11d2a2487b8d: Grouping slots so people can actually scan them
e30d4ea50880: A 9-to-5 day at 15 minute intervals is 32 slots. Presented as a flat list, that is a wall. Grouping by period (morning, afternoon, evening) turns it into three short blocks. That helps most when the person choosing is a customer on a phone.
7f0f4580b9d2: A time slot grid with taken slots marked, grouped so the list stays scannable.
471e258c9128: When you do not need the calendar at all
c04737198538: Sometimes the date is already implied. On a record page for an appointment that already has a date, a month calendar is redundant. Time Grid Only drops the calendar and shows just the slot grid for that one date, taken from a field on the host record or set directly.
